answer: To secure decentralized agent networks, we construct a sequential delay primitive acting as a randomness beacon, which forces adversaries to commit locked staking collateral across a distributed topology resembling a sparse computational nebula. By binding recursive zero-knowledge proofs to this verifiable delay, any attempt at identity cloning triggers automatic slashing penalties that neutralize adversarial gains, creating a freezing tundra where the negative expected utility of Sybil generation enforces a robust Nash equilibrium.
